ideas.name: 1. Tax-located trend leverage: the benchmark's own Nasdaq-100 engine routed through Korean tax buckets (exemption-sized TQQQ slice + ISA 2x ETF + KIS micro futures)
ideas.mechanism: No new alpha is claimed. The return engine is exactly the benchmark's: equity premium levered about 3x, protected by a 200-day trend filter. The edge is structural. Korean tax law charges the same Nasdaq-100 exposure very differently by wrapper: (a) US-listed TQQQ: 22% above 2.5M KRW a year; (b) overseas futures: 11% above a separate 2.5M KRW a year, netted with domestic index derivatives, no loss carry-forward; (c) ISA: 9.9% above 2M KRW, charged only at termination, with full loss netting inside the account; (d) FX gains on plain USD cash: 0%; (e) Korea-listed overseas ETF in a general account: 15.4% with no loss offset, and comprehensive taxation once such income passes 20M KRW (the worst bucket at size, so it is not used). Futures also finance at near-interbank rates instead of a 0.8-0.95% fund fee plus swap spread, and cost roughly 0.002% per trade instead of 0.07-0.25%. Other side of the trade: nobody. The gain comes from the tax code and fund fees, so it persists until the law changes. A large or foreign investor cannot use it; a small Korean account can, because the three exemptions (2.5M + 2.5M + 2M KRW) are large relative to its gains.
ideas.instruments: Signal: Nasdaq-100 index (^NDX). Kiwoom US account: TQQQ (3x), slice capped at 12.5M KRW; reserve collateral in SGOV or USD cash. Kiwoom ISA: TIGER 미국나스닥100레버리지(합성) 418660 (2x daily, unhedged, total fee 0.25%, net assets about 679bn KRW, listed 2022-02-22); cash leg TIGER KOFR금리액티브(합성) 449170 (verify code). KIS overseas futures account: CME Micro E-mini Nasdaq-100 (MNQ, 2 USD x index, quarterly), USD cash margin. Example size: at NDX 25,000 and USD/KRW 1,357, one MNQ is about 50,000 USD, or 68M KRW of exposure. Not used: domestic margin loans (6-9% interest, and leveraged ETFs cannot be bought on credit), currency-hedged (H) classes, and Korea-listed overseas ETFs in the general account.
ideas.rule:
1) Signal, daily after US close t: ON if NDX close(t) > simple average of the last 200 closes; else OFF. No band and no other parameter, identical to the benchmark.
2) Delay: MNQ and TQQQ orders go in the last 15 minutes of US session t+1 (marketable limits). 418660 trades in the KRX closing auction of the first Korean session ending after US close t; in the backtest, fill it at US close t+1.
3) Capital location, set on the first KRX day of each January and at each OFF-to-ON switch: V_T = min(Equity, 12.5M KRW) in TQQQ. V_I = min(Equity - V_T, available ISA contribution room; 20M KRW a year) in the ISA. V_F = the remainder, as the futures sleeve: USD margin at KIS equal to 2.5 x exchange initial margin per contract, rest in SGOV at Kiwoom.
4) Target exposure when ON: N* = 3.0 x Equity. Contracts n = round((N* - 3 x V_T - 2 x V_I) / (2 x NDX x USDKRW)), n >= 0, and futures exposure <= 4.0 x V_F (else n - 1).
5) Leverage upkeep at each US close: Lev = total exposure / Equity. If Lev > 3.5, cut one contract next session. If Lev < 2.5 and the cap allows, add one. TQQQ and 418660 reset themselves daily.
6) OFF: TQQQ to SGOV, 418660 to the KOFR ETF, all MNQ closed.
7) Roll MNQ on the Monday before the third Friday of Mar/Jun/Sep/Dec, at the US close.
8) Margin: if KIS excess margin < 1.5 x maintenance, sell SGOV and wire USD back up to 2.5 x initial; if no reserve is left, cut one contract.
9) Year-end, on a US trading day between 20 and 24 December so settlement falls inside the tax year: (i) TQQQ: if realised gains for the year are below 2.5M KRW and the open lot shows a gain, sell and immediately rebuy enough shares to bring realised gains to 2.5M (Korea has no wash-sale rule). If realised gains exceed 2.5M and open lots show losses, sell and rebuy them. (ii) Same logic on MNQ against the separate 2.5M derivatives deduction. (iii) ISA: after the 3-year minimum, terminate and reopen once the cycle's net gain exceeds 2M KRW.
10) Pre-registered measure: after-tax terminal wealth of this routing divided by that of 100% TQQQ on the same signal, 2026 Korean tax rules, at 10M, 50M and 100M KRW. Primary L* = 3.0, secondary L* = 2.0. Pass = uplift of at least 1.5 points a year at 100M and ratio above 1 in at least 70% of rolling 10-year windows.
ideas.data: Yahoo: ^NDX daily from 1985-10; QQQ from 1999-03 (dividends); TQQQ from 2010-02; NQ=F and MNQ=F for basis checks; 418660.KS from 2022-02. FRED: DTB3 and DFF (financing), SOFR (2018+), DEXKOUS (USD/KRW daily, 1981+). Before listing dates use synthetic wrappers: daily-reset Lx = L x index total return - (L-1) x (T-bill + 0.5%) - fee (0.95% for 3x; 0.25% plus an assumed 1.0% swap cost for the Korean 2x). Futures = index price return - (T-bill + 0.4%), with T-bill earned only on collateral held in bills and 0% on margin left at KIS. Bias notes: index-level data only, so no single-stock survivorship bias. ^NDX is a price index (add QQQ dividends; assume 0.3% a year before 1999). The Korean 2x ETF and MNQ tracking costs are assumptions until checked against 2022-2026 actuals. Taxes are simulated with 2026 rules and fixed nominal deductions.
ideas.testable_to_2014: Partly. The signal and exposure are testable on 1985-2014 with synthetic wrappers, holdout 2015-2026. The real instruments are newer: TQQQ Feb 2010, MNQ May 2019 (E-mini NQ 1999), 418660 Feb 2022, and the current brokerage-type ISA from 2021. The pre-2014 test therefore validates the engine and the tax arithmetic, not the instruments; instrument tracking can only be checked in the holdout.
ideas.expected_net:
Engine (trend-filtered NDX at 3x): assume 1x excess return 7.5% a year and variance 0.021 (vol 14.5%, Sharpe about 0.52). Growth = 3 x 7.5% - 9 x 0.021 / 2 + 3.5% cash = 16.5%, less 1.5-2% running costs = about 15% before tax (range 6-25%).
Benchmark tax at 100M KRW: arithmetic mean about 22%, vol about 38%, so the expected positive-year gain is about 28.6M. Tax = 22% x (28.6 - 2.5) = 5.7M, or 5.7 points a year, with no carry-forward of loss years. Benchmark net is about 11% (range 4-19%).
This routing at 100M (TQQQ 12.5M, ISA 20M, futures sleeve 67.5M with 3 MNQ): tax = 0.24M (TQQQ slice) + 0.23M a year (ISA: 9.9% x (9M - 2M) per 3-year cycle) + 1.86M (futures: 11% x (19.4M - 2.5M)) = 2.3M, or 2.3 points. Tax saved is about 3.4 points. Non-tax items roughly cancel: idle margin at KIS costs 0.75-1.25 points; lower financing and commissions give back 1.0-2.0 points.
Net: about 13.5-14.5% a year (range 6-23%), an uplift of 2 to 3.5 points at 30-100M KRW and about zero at 10M. Net Sharpe before tax 0.45-0.65. Maximum drawdown -60% to -80%; a 1987-type -15% day is -45% in one session at 3x.
ideas.capital_fit: 10M KRW: no edge. The 2.5M exemption already makes 100% TQQQ almost tax-free up to a 25% yearly gain, and one MNQ would be about 7x leverage, so the method collapses to the benchmark. 30M: TQQQ 12.5M + ISA 17.5M, total leverage about 2.4x, tax saving about 3 points, no futures. 50M: TQQQ 12.5M + ISA 20M + 1 MNQ on a 17.5M sleeve, total about 2.9x; workable but lumpy, since one contract is the whole futures leg. 100M: TQQQ 12.5M + ISA 20M + 3 MNQ, total about 2.8x; the best fit.
ideas.fake_risks: 1) It is not alpha. If the engine has a bad decade, this only loses less tax; the engine risk is fully shared with the benchmark. 2) Tax law: an August 2026 reform bill would cap a general ISA at 5 years and end carry-over of unused room from 2027; the derivatives rate has been raised before; a financial investment income tax was legislated once and repealed. 3) Interest on USD futures margin at KIS is assumed to be 0% and is unverified; margin kept at 3x initial or more costs over 1 point a year. 4) Futures do not reset daily and come in 68M KRW lumps, so leverage drifts, a gap can force liquidation, and KIS can raise margins overnight. 5) The Korean 2x ETF is swap-based; its true drag and its premium or discount in Korean hours must be measured on 2022-2026 data. 6) Year-end sell-and-rebuy relies on settlement-date tax treatment and the absence of a wash-sale rule. 7) Leveraged-product rules were tightened repeatedly in 2026 (deposits, education, mock trading). 8) The pre-2014 test is synthetic.

ideas.name: 2. KOSPI200 night shift: hold 2x Korea only from the closing auction to the next opening auction
ideas.mechanism: Published decompositions show Korean equity returns accruing while the Korean market is closed. Knuteson (arXiv 2010.01727) reports for the KOSPI Composite, July 1997 to September 2020, a cumulative overnight (close-to-open) return of +5,246% against an intraday return of -94%. My annualisation: about +18.7% a year overnight and -11.4% a year intraday, or +0.069% per night. A 2023 Finance Research Letters study of KOSPI200 firms (2008-2022) finds overnight over-reaction with daytime reversal, with individuals trading against the overnight move and institutions and foreigners with it. Economic story: Korea is a price-taker of the European and US sessions, so the equity premium and most news arrive while Korea is shut, and whoever carries inventory through the night bears gap risk and is paid for it. Other side: Korean day-traders and intraday liquidity demanders who buy at or after the open and flatten before the close. Why it could persist: it is a risk premium, not an arbitrage. Why a small Korean account is suited: KODEX 레버리지 gains are effectively untaxed, ETFs carry no transaction tax, commission is about 0.013%, and auction fills at 10-100M KRW have no market impact.
ideas.instruments: Primary: KODEX 레버리지 122630 (2x daily KOSPI200, fee 0.64%), Kiwoom general account. Its gains are taxed at 15.4% on the smaller of the trading gain and the rise in the tax-base price, which excludes domestic stock and domestic listed-futures gains, so the tax is close to zero in practice; confirm in the first live month. Test proxy: KODEX 200 069500. Secondary, only after the ETF test passes and capital is at least about 30M KRW: mini KOSPI200 futures at KIS (50,000 KRW x index; 11% tax above 2.5M; 10M KRW basic deposit, education and mock trading required).
ideas.rule:
Primary rule P0, no signal and no parameters:
1) Every KRX trading day at 15:19 KST, send a market buy order into the closing call auction (15:20-15:30) for floor(sleeve equity / last price) shares of 122630.
2) Next trading day at 08:55 KST, send a market sell order for the whole position into the opening call auction (fills at 09:00). Hold KRW cash intraday. Repeat.
3) Kill switch: stop if trailing 250-night net return is below -15%, or if all-in cost per side rises above 0.03%.
Returns: overnight(t) = (Open(t) + cash distribution on ex-date t) / Close(t-1) - 1. Cost model: 0.013% commission + 0.01% slippage per side = 0.046% per night; stress at 0.07%.
Pre-registered gates:
Train (069500, 2002-10-14 to 2014-12-30; 122630 from 2010): G1, mean overnight minus mean intraday log return has a Newey-West t-statistic of at least 3. G2, synthetic 2x night-only (2 x overnight - 0.046% - 0.64%/252) grows at least 8% a year net and at least as fast as buy-and-hold 2x. G3, net positive in at least 9 of 12 calendar years. If any gate fails, stop and do not open the holdout.
Holdout (actual 122630, 2015-01 to date), run once: net growth at least 6% a year, net Sharpe at least 0.5, positive over the last 3 years.
Then 3 months of paper fills against published open and close, then live at no more than 25% of capital until 250 live nights exist.
Reported but not selectable after the fact: P1, hold the night only if 069500 close(t-1) is above its 200-day average at t-1 (one-day lag). P2, mini futures at 3x: buy at the 15:45 close, sell at the 08:45 open, n = floor(3 x equity / (50,000 x KOSPI200)).
ideas.data: Yahoo: 069500.KS daily open and close from 2002-10-14, 122630.KS from 2010-02-22, plus the distribution history for 069500. ^KS11 and ^KS200 only as cross-checks. No survivorship bias: one index, instruments that still exist, no selection. The real data risk is the Open field: it must be the 09:00 auction price. Verify a sample against a second free source, such as the broker's own daily chart API or the KRX Open API (free key, 10,000 calls a day; history depth not confirmed). Index opens are not tradable prints and must not be used for the decision. Futures history is not on Yahoo, so P2 needs the KRX key.
ideas.testable_to_2014: Yes for the ETF version: 069500 gives about 3,000 nights in 2002-2014 and 122630 gives 2010-2014, leaving 2015-2026 as a blind holdout. Mini KOSPI200 futures were listed only in July 2015 (full-size 1996), so the futures variant is post-2014 for the mini contract and depends on obtaining the KRX key.
ideas.expected_net:
Per night on the 2x ETF: net = 2 x m - 0.046%, where m is the tradable 1x overnight mean. Break-even m = 0.023% (about 5.7% a year). Cost alone is 0.046% x 247 = 11.4% a year (6.4% with commission only).
ETF scenarios, with overnight vol about 11% at 1x:
A) Full strength, m = 0.069% (17.1% log a year): 2 x 17.1 - 1.2 (variance) - 11.4 - 0.6 = about +21% a year.
B) Half strength (8.5%): 17 - 1.2 - 11.4 - 0.6 = about +4%.
C) No effect (4%): about -5%.
My weights are A 20-25%, B 40%, C 35-40%, giving an unconditional expectation of about +3 to +5% a year. That is not worth deploying untested.
Conditional on passing every gate: 10-18% a year untaxed, vol about 22%, Sharpe 0.5-0.8, drawdown -40% to -60% (October 2008 had repeated -5% to -8% gaps).
Futures at 3x with about 0.01% cost per night on notional (assumed commission): A) 3 x 17.7 - 5.4 - 7.5 = 40% before tax, about 35% after 11%. B) about 13%. C) about 1%.
Scenario A in futures is the only route in this report to the investor's 30%+ wish. I put it at 10-15%, and it needs at least 30M KRW.
ideas.capital_fit: 10M KRW: mechanically fine (the ETF is very liquid), but leveraged ETFs carry a 10M KRW basic-deposit rule, so an account at exactly 10M may be blocked from buying after its first loss; practical minimum 12-15M or a broker waiver. 50M: ETF version fine; 1-2 mini futures possible. 100M: both fine; auction size is immaterial. The futures variant needs about 30M or more: one mini contract is 50,000 x index (37M KRW at 740), plus the 10M basic deposit.
ideas.fake_risks: 1) The headline numbers are for an index, not a tradable price. Stock opening auctions may overshoot in a way an ETF or future does not, so the tradable effect could be half or less; this is the main reason for my low confidence. 2) Knuteson's own footnote says the US divergence stopped after 2008; Korea may have followed. 3) With about 247 round trips a year, a 0.01% change in cost per side moves the result by about 5 points a year. 4) ETF market makers have no quoting duty in the auctions, so fills can deviate from fair value. 5) Regime change: KRX night futures since June 2025, Nextrade pre-market since 2025, KRX after-market since 14 September 2026 (ETFs excluded), KRX pre-market planned for 2027. Price discovery is moving outside the regular session and may erode or relocate the premium. 6) Leveraged-ETF rebalancing pushes the close in the day's direction, which contaminates entry prices. 7) Yahoo open-price errors and unadjusted distributions can manufacture the effect. 8) Auction failures on limit-move, sidecar or outage days. 9) Unlike a trend-filtered position, it takes every overnight crash.

ideas.name: 3. Dual-market 2x momentum switch with a tax-free Korean leg (KOSPI200 2x vs Nasdaq-100 2x vs cash)
ideas.mechanism: Two documented effects, time-series momentum and cross-market relative momentum, combined with a Korean tax asymmetry. Other side: slow capital that under-reacts to persistent moves, and in Korea specifically retail contrarians who sell rallies and buy inverse-2x ETFs into them. The Korean leg (KODEX 레버리지) pays close to 0% tax and 0.013% commission; the US leg sits in the ISA at 9.9%, deferred and with loss netting. Whenever Korea is the stronger market, gains compound untaxed, which lowers the after-tax hurdle for holding Korea. The unhedged US leg also carries USD exposure, which tends to rise against the won when equities fall (on 6 November 2026 KOSPI fell 6.0% and USD/KRW rose 14.5 won). The momentum effects are widely known and can be dormant for years. The tax asymmetry persists while the tax-base-price rule stands.
ideas.instruments: Korea leg: KODEX 레버리지 122630, in both the ISA and the general account. US leg in the ISA: TIGER 미국나스닥100레버리지(합성) 418660 (2x, unhedged). US leg in the general account: TQQQ at 2/3 weight with 1/3 in SGOV (equals 2x) for the first 15M KRW, so gains stay near the 2.5M exemption; above that, MNQ under the rules of method 1 if capital allows, otherwise 418660. Cash leg: TIGER KOFR금리액티브(합성) 449170 in KRW accounts (verify code); SGOV if coming out of TQQQ. All at Kiwoom; KIS only if MNQ is used.
ideas.rule:
Decision day D = last KRX trading day of each month, using closes up to D-1 (one-day lag).
1) R_K = KOSPI (^KS11) 252-trading-day price return.
2) R_N = (NDX x USD/KRW) 252-day return.
3) R_C = compounded 91-day CD rate over the same window.
4) Trend flags: T_K = KOSPI close > its 200-day average; T_N = NDX (in USD) close > its 200-day average.
5) Rank K and N by R. Hold the first one with R > R_C and its flag true. If neither qualifies, hold cash.
6) Between month-ends, check daily: if the held market closes below its 200-day average, sell at the next close and stay in cash until the next month-end decision. No intra-month re-entry.
7) Execution: Korean ETFs in the KRX closing auction on D; TQQQ at the following US close. Position is 100% of each account in the mapped instrument; no margin loans.
8) Tax upkeep as in method 1, step 9: December sell-and-rebuy of TQQQ up to the 2.5M exemption; ISA termination and reopening after 3 years.
9) Pre-registered test: 252-day lookback and 200-day filter are fixed, not optimised. Train 1997-07 to 2014-12, holdout 2015 to date. Compare after-tax terminal wealth with the benchmark and with a 2x Nasdaq-only version. Keep the method only if it beats the Nasdaq-only version in the training period by at least 1 point a year after tax.
ideas.data: Yahoo: ^KS11 daily from 1997-07; 069500.KS (2002-10+) and 122630.KS (2010-02+) to calibrate the synthetic 2x; ^NDX (1985+), QQQ (1999+), TQQQ (2010+), 418660.KS (2022+). FRED: DEXKOUS (USD/KRW daily, 1981+), the Korean 3-month CD rate (OECD monthly series, 1991+), DTB3. Synthetic 2x Korea before 2010 = 2 x daily index return - (CD rate + 0.64%) / 252, calibrated on 2010-2014 actuals. Bias notes: index-level only, so no single-stock survivorship bias. KOSPI is a price index, so dividends of about 1.5% a year are omitted (conservative). The training window starts in the 1997-98 crisis, which flatters any trend filter on Korea.
ideas.testable_to_2014: Yes for signals and synthetic 2x returns (1997-07 to 2014-12, holdout 2015-2026). Instruments: 122630 from February 2010 and TQQQ from February 2010 are real before 2014; 418660 (February 2022) and the current ISA (2021) are not, so the US leg and its ISA tax treatment are synthetic before 2014.
ideas.expected_net:
Engine at 2x: assume blended 1x excess return 6.5% a year and variance 0.021. Growth = 2 x 6.5% - 4 x 0.021 / 2 + 3% cash = 11.8%, less about 1% costs = about 11% before tax (range 4-18%). Tax: Korean-leg gains about 0%, ISA 9.9% deferred, TQQQ slice mostly inside the exemption, so about 0.3-0.8 points. Net about 10% a year (range 4-17%). Net Sharpe 0.45-0.6; maximum drawdown -55% to -75%.
Against the benchmark (about 11% at 100M KRW, about 13% at 10M where the benchmark is almost untaxed), it wins only if Korea has strong, trending multi-year runs like 2025 to May 2026, or if 3x proves to be over-betting.
ideas.capital_fit: 10M KRW: fits entirely inside Kiwoom with no futures, subject to the 10M basic-deposit rule on leveraged ETFs. This is the only method here that is structurally different from the benchmark at 10M, though not likely better. 50M: fits; ISA 20M plus general account. 100M: fits; route the US leg above ISA room through MNQ as in method 1 to avoid the 15.4% no-offset bucket.
ideas.fake_risks: 1) Capped at 2x against the benchmark's 3x; if the Nasdaq trend stays strong it will lag. 2) KOSPI's long-run Sharpe is low. A 1997-2014 training window (crisis rebound, 2003-07 boom) is favourable to Korea and the 2015-2024 holdout is not; expect an unstable verdict. 3) A two-asset relative-momentum switch has very few independent decisions (one every 1-2 years), so the backtest has little statistical power. 4) The near-zero tax on 122630 depends on the tax-base-price rule and must be confirmed on actual statements. 5) FX conversion and US commissions on each Korea-to-US switch. 6) The 2025-26 Korean rally and the subsequent fall (KOSPI about 7,500 in May 2026, 5,060 on 6 November 2026) will dominate the holdout and can make it look either brilliant or terrible depending on exit timing.

top_pick:
Method 1, tax-located trend leverage. It is the only one whose advantage does not rest on a forecast: it holds the same exposure as the benchmark and pays about 3.4 points a year less tax on a 30-100M KRW account (5.7 points of capital a year falls to about 2.3 at 100M), plus cheaper financing and trading. It should be read as a 2 to 3.5 point improvement on an engine I expect to compound at roughly 10-17% a year net, not as a route to 30-60%. At 10M KRW it gives nothing, because the 2.5M exemption already makes plain TQQQ nearly tax-free; at that size the benchmark itself is the right holding.

Rank reflects probability times size of uplift, which is why method 2 sits above method 3 despite lower confidence. Test method 2 first: it needs two free price series and has no parameters, and it is the only item with a path (which I put at 10-15%) to 25-35% a year, via the futures variant. If it fails its training gates, drop it without opening the holdout. Method 3 is the fallback for an account too small for futures that wants a Korean leg.
honest_ceiling:
Realistic long-run net growth for this investor is 10-17% a year, central estimate about 13%, with drawdowns of -50% to -80%. The wished-for 30-60% is not reachable by any method I can honestly specify from free daily data.

Arithmetic. With known parameters and continuous rebalancing, maximum log growth is g = r + S^2/2, where S is the true net Sharpe ratio, and the portfolio's volatility at that point equals S.
- Leveraged index beta with a trend filter realistically has S = 0.45-0.65 after costs. S^2/2 = 10-21%, plus r of about 3% gives 13-24% before tax at full Kelly.
- Parameters are not known, so the prudent bet is half to three-quarters Kelly, which keeps 75-94% of the excess: about 10.5-22% before tax.
- Korean tax takes 11-22% of gains above small deductions with no loss carry-forward. Tax location (method 1) cuts the drag from about 4-5 points to about 1.5-2.5 points. Result: about 10-17% net.
- Repeating the 2010-2025 Nasdaq decade (trend-filtered Sharpe near 0.9) gave 25-30% net. That is the top-decile outcome, not the expectation.

What 30-60% would require. Net +30% is 26% log growth, which needs about 30% before tax, so S^2/2 = 27% and S = 0.73, run at full Kelly with about 73% annual volatility. Net +60% is 47% log growth, needing S of about 1.0 at about 100% volatility, with no estimation error. No retail method on free daily data has a dependable net Sharpe of 0.75-1.0 at that scale. The only candidate here is the futures variant of method 2 in its full-strength scenario (about 35% net), which I put at 10-15% probability before testing.

Leverage caution. Kelly leverage is excess return divided by variance. At my central estimate (7.5% / 0.021) it is 3.6x, so 3x is roughly full Kelly. If the true excess return is 4%, Kelly is 1.9x and 3x is over-betting: growth is 3 x 4% - 9.45% = 2.6% at 3x against 2 x 4% - 4.2% = 3.8% at 2x. At the central estimate, 2x still earns about 83% of the 3x growth (10.8% against 13.0%). For a 10-30 year horizon, 2-2.5x is the more defensible choice.
assumptions_challenged:
1) "Korea-listed leveraged ETFs pay 15.4% on gains." This is true only for overseas underlyings. For domestic-equity leveraged and inverse ETFs (KODEX 레버리지, KOSDAQ150 2x, the inverse 2x), tax is 15.4% on the smaller of the trading gain and the rise in the tax-base price, and that price ignores domestic stock and domestic listed-futures gains. A January 2026 press article calls the result "effectively tax-free", and one unverified forum comment cites KODEX 반도체레버리지 trading near 25,000 KRW against a tax-base price near 9,900. This is the largest Korea-specific asymmetry: a 2x long or short position on Korean indices with almost no tax and 0.013% commission. It must be confirmed on the investor's own tax statements.

2) "Tax drag is the main problem." It depends on size. At 10M KRW the 2.5M deduction shelters a 25% yearly gain, so US-listed 3x is nearly untaxed and tax engineering adds nothing. At 50-100M the drag is 5-6 points of capital a year and wrapper choice matters more than any signal tweak. A research team that tests at one capital level will reach the wrong conclusion for the other.

3) "Domestic margin is useful leverage." Margin loans cost 6-9% against roughly 3% implied in futures, and leveraged ETFs cannot be bought on credit. It is the most expensive leverage available and should not be used. The ISA is more valuable for taxed assets than for domestic equity that is untaxed anyway.

4) "An index open is a tradable price." Overnight-versus-intraday studies use index opens built from individual stock auctions. Any Korean overnight result must be re-derived on ETF or futures auction prices before it is believed.

5) "Hedge the currency." For a won-based investor, unhedged USD exposure is a diversifier: the won tends to weaken when equities fall, FX gains on plain USD cash are untaxed, and hedging costs the rate differential. Unhedged classes and USD collateral are the better default.

6) "Korea-specific alpha exists for small accounts." The durable ones (IPO equal-allocation subscriptions, SPACs bought near trust value, mispriced rights) are capacity-limited, manual, not testable before 2014 and do not compound. On my rough estimate IPO allocations are worth perhaps 0.3-1.0M KRW a year per account: meaningful on 10M, negligible on 100M. Year-end large-shareholder tax selling gives one trade a year in a regime that has changed five times.

7) "More leverage means more growth." See the Kelly arithmetic in the ceiling section; the benchmark's 3x is not obviously better than 2x over 10-30 years.

Not verified, and to be checked before coding: whether single-stock futures are outside the 11% derivatives tax (I did not rely on it); interest paid on USD futures margin at KIS (assumed 0%); KIS commissions on MNQ and mini KOSPI200; whether the 10M KRW leveraged-ETF deposit rule applies inside an ISA; history depth of the KRX Open API; current NDX and KOSPI200 levels for contract sizing.

ideas.name: 1. ISA volatility-scaled trend ladder on the Nasdaq-100 (cash / 1x / 2x Korea-listed ETFs)
ideas.mechanism:
Not alpha in the hedge-fund sense. Three sources, in order of certainty.
(a) Tax and cost location (certain while the law stands). Inside the ISA all gains and losses are netted over the contract period, only the net above 2M KRW is taxed at 9.9%, and the tax is deferred. A US-listed leveraged ETF is taxed 22% on every good calendar year with no loss carry-forward, which for a 45%-volatility strategy costs roughly 4pp of log growth a year at 100M KRW. Korea-listed ETF commission is about 0.015% against 0.25%. The other side is the tax code, not a trader.
(b) Variance timing. Growth-optimal leverage is L = (expected excess return) / variance. Volatility clusters and is far more predictable than returns, so a fixed 2x or 3x holder is over-levered exactly when variance is high. S&P 500 1928-2015: volatility 14.7% above the 200-day average versus 26.5% below; return +14.1% versus -2.3% (Gayed and Bilello, checked via a secondary summary). Supporting papers, quoted from memory and not re-checked: Moreira and Muir 2017, Harvey et al. 2018; disputed out of sample by Cederburg et al. 2020. The other side is constant-leverage holders and funds that must re-lever mechanically. Dip buyers are paid a liquidity premium when we de-lever, which is why this edge is modest. It should persist because clustering is a property of volatility, not a price anomaly.
(c) Trend gating. Bear markets unfold slowly (slow news diffusion, forced de-leveraging). The other side is contrarian buyers and policy support, which produce V-shaped recoveries and whipsaws. This is the weakest leg; its value rests on a few episodes (1929-32, 2000-02, 2008).
The base return is the equity risk premium, paid by savers and hedgers who shed equity risk.
ideas.instruments:

- 2x: TIGER 미국나스닥100레버리지(합성), code 418660. Twice the daily Nasdaq-100 return, currency-unhedged, fee 0.25%, net assets about 679bn KRW on 2026-11-10, listed 2022-02-22.
- 1x: TIGER 미국나스닥100 (133690), or KODEX 미국나스닥100 (379810).
- Cash: KODEX CD금리액티브(합성) (459580), or KODEX KOFR금리액티브(합성) (423160).
- Signal series: QQQ dividend-adjusted close (Yahoo); cash rate FRED DTB3.
Overflow, only for money that cannot enter the ISA and cannot use method 2: Kiwoom overseas account with QQQM (1x), QLD (2x), TQQQ (3x), SGOV (cash); cap 3x; 22% tax.
Robustness variant, not primary: TIGER 미국S&P500 (360750) plus TIGER 미국S&P500레버리지(합성 H) (225040). The 2x fund is currency-hedged and thin (net assets about 55bn KRW, a few thousand shares a day).
Why the Nasdaq-100 here: it is the only liquid, unhedged 2x US-index fund on the Korean exchange, and its higher volatility means the 2x cap binds less often. This is a vehicle decision, not a forecast that the Nasdaq-100 will outperform.
ideas.rule:
Run once per US trading day after the US close of day t (about 07:00 KST).
1. Series: P = QQQ dividend-adjusted close; r_d = P_d / P_(d-1) - 1; cash = FRED DTB3 compounded daily.
2. Trend score T_t = average of three 0/1 flags: (a) P_t above its 200-day simple mean; (b) 126-day return of P above the 126-day cash return; (c) 252-day return of P above the 252-day cash return. T is 0, 1/3, 2/3 or 1.
3. Volatility forecast: v_t = lambda * v_(t-1) + (1 - lambda) * r_t^2, with lambda = 0.5^(1/20) = 0.9659 (20-trading-day half-life), seeded with the mean of r^2 over the first 60 days. sigma_t = sqrt(252 * v_t). Require 252 days of history before the first trade.
4. Target leverage L*_t = T_t * min(CAP, 0.40 / sigma_t). CAP = 2 in the ISA, 3 in the overflow account. The 0.40 risk target is fixed in advance: about three-quarters Kelly on a prior in-trend Sharpe of 0.53 (history 0.8, shrunk by a third). It must not be optimised.
5. Holdings for L*. If L* <= 1: 1x weight = L*, cash weight = 1 - L*. If 1 < L* <= 2: 2x weight = L* - 1, 1x weight = 2 - L*. Overflow only, 2 < L* <= 3: 3x weight = L* - 2, 2x weight = 3 - L*.
6. No-trade band. L_now = (value of 1x + 2 * value of 2x + 3 * value of 3x) / account value. Trade to the step-5 weights only if |L* - L_now| >= 0.25, or if L* = 0 while L_now > 0. Otherwise send no order.
7. Execution: next KRX session at 09:30 KST, sells before buys, marketable limit orders no worse than 0.3% from iNAV, re-quoted every 10 minutes, limit widened to 0.5% after 14:30. Never trade in the first 10 minutes or the closing auction. If the fund's premium or discount to iNAV exceeds 1%, wait one session. Overflow account: market-on-close on day t+1.
8. Exit is the same rule (T falls or sigma rises). No stops, no overrides, no re-fitting.
9. Backtest conventions. Fill at the US close of t+1, a full day late and stricter than live. Cost per side 0.10% for Korea-listed (commission plus spread and premium) and 0.27% for US-listed (rerun at 0.09%). Simulated 2x fund = 2 * daily index return - (T-bill + 0.75%)/252 on the borrowed half - 0.25%/252 fee, then multiplied by the daily USD/KRW change. ISA tax = 9.9% of cumulative net gain above 2M KRW at each settlement (run both 3-year and 5-year cycles), then re-entry at 20M KRW a year with the remainder on the overflow route. Overflow tax = 22% of each calendar year's net realised gain above 2.5M KRW, paid the following May, losses not carried forward. Run at 10M, 50M and 100M KRW because the exemptions are fixed won amounts.

ideas.expected_net:
Not measured; arithmetic on stated priors.
Shrunk case: Nasdaq-100 in-trend excess return 10% a year (history about 15%), in market about 70% of days. The 2x cap binds when forecast volatility is at or below 20% (about 60% of in-trend days, average volatility 15.5%); otherwise average volatility 27% and L about 1.5.
- Capped state: 2 * 10% - 0.5 * 4 * 0.155^2 = 20 - 4.8 = 15.2%.
- Uncapped state: 1.48 * 10% - 0.5 * 0.40^2 = 14.8 - 8.0 = 6.8%.
- Blend: 0.6 * 15.2 + 0.4 * 6.8 = 11.8%; times 0.70 in market = 8.3% a year.
- Less one-day delay and whipsaw 1.0, fund fee and swap spread 0.7, trading 0.8 = 5.8%. Plus cash about 3% = 8.8% pre-tax log growth.
- ISA tax about 0.8pp. Net about 8% a year.
History repeats (in-trend excess 15%): (0.6 * 25.2 + 0.4 * 14.2) * 0.70 = 14.6; minus 2.5, plus 3 = 15.1% pre-tax; net about 13.5-14.5%.
Repeat of 2010-2025 (in-trend excess 22%): about 23-26% net.
Range to quote: 8-14% net a year, about 25% only in a repeat of the best era. Sharpe 0.45-0.6, annual volatility about 28-32%, worst drawdown -55% to -70%. A 1987-type -20% day at 2x is -40% in one session.
Benchmark on the same shrunk inputs (TQQQ with a 200-day filter, Kiwoom, 22% tax): (3 * 10% - 0.5 * 9 * 0.18^2) * 0.70 = 10.8; minus 1.0 delay, 1.65 fee and swap, 0.7 to 2.5 commissions; plus 3.5 cash = 9.2-11.0% pre-tax. Tax drag about 4pp at 100M KRW and about 2pp at 10M. Net about 5-7% at 100M and 7-9% at 10M.
So method 1 is ahead by 1-3pp in the shrunk case, roughly level if history repeats (benchmark about 15-16% net), and behind by about 4pp in a bull repeat because of the 2x cap.
ideas.capital_fit:
10M KRW: the whole amount fits in the ISA and tax is close to zero. One real obstacle: Korea-listed leveraged ETFs require a 10M KRW basic deposit (cash plus 70% of non-leveraged holdings) at each purchase, plus prior education. At exactly 10M or after any loss the 2x rung can be blocked. Whether Kiwoom applies this inside the ISA, or relaxes it with trading history, I could not confirm. If blocked, the ladder runs at a 1x cap, or use method 2.
50M KRW: 20M a year can enter the ISA, so it takes three years to move everything in. The rest goes to method 2 or the overflow account in the meantime.
100M KRW: five years to fill at 20M a year, lifetime contribution cap 100M. The August 2026 tax proposal (not enacted, under review) would cap the contract at 5 years and end carry-over of unused limits from 2027. Realistically the ISA shelters a third to a half of the capital over time; the remainder needs method 2.
Liquidity is ample at all three sizes (the 2x fund holds about 679bn KRW).
ideas.fake_risks:
1. The 2x cap. In a strong low-volatility bull market a 3x fund compounds much faster. In the 2015-2026 holdout I expect the 3x benchmark to be ahead before tax.
2. The trend leg rests on three or four episodes. V-shaped recoveries (2019, 2020, April 2025) cost money, and combining it with volatility scaling re-enters slowly.
3. Volatility scaling cannot see a crash from calm (October 1987, February 2018, 5 November 2026 when the S&P 500 fell 4.4% in a day). Its out-of-sample value is disputed.
4. The 0.40 risk target, 20-day half-life and 0.25 band are set by prior reasoning. Any tuning on history is overfitting. Declare the sensitivity grid in advance (target 0.30/0.40/0.50, half-life 10/20/40, band 0.15/0.25/0.35) and require the result to hold across most of it.
5. Simulated 2x fund before 2022: swap spread, tracking in stress and Korean-hours premium are assumptions. Only four years of real data exist.
6. Index hindsight. The Nasdaq-100 fell 83% in 2000-02; Japan after 1989 shows a market where the same rule earns little.
7. Rule risk. ISA terms are under revision; leveraged-product rules were tightened twice in 2026.
8. Currency. The fund is unhedged, so a stronger won reduces returns.
Pre-registered pass test: net-of-tax log growth above both the 3x-trend benchmark and 1x buy-and-hold on at least two of three pre-2015 data sets (US market 1926-2014, Nasdaq-100 1985-2014, pooled other countries), then open the holdout once.

ideas.name: 2. Volatility-scaled trend exposure with CME E-nano and Micro S&P 500 futures (cap 3x, 11% tax)
ideas.mechanism:
The same engine as method 1 (equity premium, variance timing, trend gating), in a different wrapper.
Structural edge versus a US-listed 3x ETF:
- Tax is 11% instead of 22%, with a separate 2.5M KRW exemption.
- No fund fee (about 0.9% a year on a 3x ETF).
- Financing at the futures-implied rate, roughly the dollar overnight rate plus 0.3-0.6%, instead of swap spreads inside a fund.
- Commissions of about 1-3 basis points of notional instead of 0.25% of capital per switch.
- Leverage can be set to any level, so the position can follow L = 0.40 / volatility exactly instead of jumping between 0x and 3x.
The other side of the financing is dealers and arbitrageurs who rent balance sheet; that market is deep and persistent.
The offsetting cost is idle margin. Futures charge financing on the whole notional, so collateral sitting at the broker at 0% loses the cash rate. With 60% of capital idle at a 3.5% cash rate that is about 2.1% a year, more than the ETF fee it avoids. The method is cheaper than the benchmark only if part of the collateral earns interest.

- NES, E-nano S&P 500: USD 0.50 x index, about USD 3,775 or 5.1M KRW per contract. Listed by CME from 2026-08-24, quarterly cycle, tick 0.5 point = USD 0.25, cash settled.
- Reserve: won money-market ETF at Kiwoom (459580 or 423160), inside the ISA if there is room.
- Signal: SPY dividend-adjusted close (Yahoo); cash rate FRED DTB3.

Not verified: whether KIS lists the E-nano contracts, the KIS commission per contract, and whether KIS pays interest on margin deposits. The KIS pages could not be read. Retail access to overseas derivatives requires one hour of education and three hours of mock trading (since 2025-12-15); there is no basic deposit.
ideas.rule:
Steps 1-4 of method 1 with P = SPY dividend-adjusted close and CAP = 3, so L*_t = T_t * min(3, 0.40 / sigma_t).
5. Sleeve equity E (KRW) = KIS futures account equity + reserve. Contract value: MES = 5 * F * USDKRW; NES = 0.5 * F * USDKRW, where F is the front futures price. Target notional X = L* * E. n_MES = floor(X / MES value). n_NES = round((X - n_MES * MES value) / NES value). If NES is not available: n_MES = round(X / MES value).
6. No-trade band: L_now = current notional / E. Change the position only if |L* - L_now| >= 0.25, or if L* = 0 with a position on.
7. Execution: market order or one-tick marketable limit in the front quarterly contract when Globex reopens after the daily break that follows the signal close (07:00 or 08:00 KST depending on daylight saving).
8. Roll: on the second Thursday of each expiry month (eight days before the third-Friday expiry) move every contract to the next quarter.
9. Collateral: keep 60% of E in the KIS account and 40% in the reserve. If KIS equity falls below 45% of E, top up to 60% (the program alerts; the transfer may need a manual step). Above 75%, sweep back to 60%. Hard limit checked daily: initial margin of the position must not exceed 40% of KIS equity; otherwise cut contracts until it does.
10. Tax reserve: accrue 11% of year-to-date net futures profit above 2.5M KRW inside the reserve; pay in May.
11. Exit is the same rule. No stops, no overrides.
12. Backtest conventions. Fill at the US close of t+1. Futures daily return = index total return - (T-bill + 0.40%)/252. Cost per side = half a tick plus commission (assume USD 1.0 per MES and USD 0.5 per NES until the KIS schedule is confirmed). Roll cost one tick, four times a year. 60% of E earns 0%; 40% earns the Korean CD rate less 15.4%. Rerun with all collateral at 0% and all at the T-bill rate. Profit and loss converted at daily USD/KRW with 0.2% cost on amounts actually converted. Tax 11% of calendar-year net futures profit above 2.5M KRW, no loss carry-forward. Run at 10M, 50M and 100M KRW with whole-contract rounding.

ideas.fake_risks:
1. Collateral interest is decisive and unverified. With all collateral idle, the cost advantage over a leveraged ETF disappears and only the tax gap remains.
2. E-nano availability at KIS, its fees and its liquidity are unconfirmed. The contract is three months old.

6. All the signal risks of method 1 apply: dependence on a few crisis episodes, whipsaw in V-shaped recoveries, parameters set by prior, disputed out-of-sample value of volatility scaling.
7. Whole-contract rounding at small capital makes realised leverage differ from target by up to 0.25x.
8. Operational: quarterly rolls, API outages during the daily maintenance break, dollar profit and loss conversion.
Same pre-registered pass test and sensitivity grid as method 1.

ideas.name: 3. Domestic low-tax sleeve: the same engine on KOSPI 200 with KODEX 200 and KODEX 레버리지 (optional, conditional)
ideas.mechanism:
The signal engine is unchanged. The distinct element is structural: Korea-listed domestic-equity ETFs carry no capital gains tax, and a domestic-index leveraged ETF is taxed at 15.4% on the lesser of the trading gain and the rise in its taxable base price. That base has in practice usually risen little, because gains on listed shares and their exchange-traded derivatives are excluded from it. A fund guide describes the resulting tax as often small; it is a practice, not a guarantee. Commission is about 0.015%, with no currency conversion and no US withholding.
The other side is again the tax code. The underlying premium is the Korean equity premium, which has historically been lower and less reliable than the US one (dilution, governance, cyclicality). A cheap wrapper does not repair a weak premium, which is why this ranks third.

10M KRW: fits, but the same 10M KRW basic deposit and education rule for Korea-listed leveraged ETFs applies, so the 2x rung can be blocked at or below 10M.
50M and 100M KRW: no constraint; both funds are among the most liquid on the exchange.
If leveraged-ETF gains ever are taxed in full they count as dividend income, and total financial income above 20M KRW a year moves into progressive rates. That matters at 100M in a strong year.
ideas.fake_risks:
1. Weak underlying premium. The tax saving of 2-4pp a year versus a taxable US 3x fund does not offset a Sharpe ratio that may be half the US one.
2. Trend rules have whipsawed badly in range-bound Korean markets (roughly 2011-2020).
3. Concentration in two semiconductor stocks; 2026 saw a surge and a -6% day on 6 November.
4. The low tax is a by-product of how the taxable base is computed. It can change, and leveraged products are under active regulatory tightening in 2026.
5. Short, single-country sample; any good result is one path.
6. The 2015-2026 holdout contains an exceptional rally, so a good holdout would say little about the future.

top_pick:
Method 1 for every won that fits in the ISA, with method 2 as the home for the rest: one signal engine, two wrappers. If only one may be named, method 1.

Why method 1 first: its advantage over a 3x trend ETF in a taxable US account does not depend on any forecast. It is the gap between 9.9% on netted, deferred gains with about 0.015% commission, and 22% on each good year with no relief for bad years and 0.25% commission. It also has no margin calls and is the simplest to automate.

Its limits: the 2x cap, the 20M KRW a year contribution limit, a proposed 5-year contract cap from 2027, and the 10M KRW basic deposit for leveraged ETFs, which can block a 10M account. That is why method 2 is needed as capital grows, and why method 2 has the higher chance (58% against 50%) of beating the 3x benchmark: it keeps 3x in calm uptrends.

Method 3 should not be funded unless it passes its own test.

No backtest was run; this is design only. Before any money:
1. Pre-register the parameters exactly as written (trend trio, 20-day half-life, 0.40 risk target, 0.25 band) and the sensitivity grid.
2. Test on data to 2014: US market 1926-2014, Nasdaq-100 1985-2014, other countries pooled, at 10M, 50M and 100M KRW, against a 3x ETF with a 200-day filter under Kiwoom costs and 22% tax.
3. Fix the pass criterion in advance: net-of-tax log growth above the benchmark on at least two of the three data sets, and no worse than the benchmark minus 2pp a year in the 2015-2026 holdout, opened once.
4. Confirm four facts with the brokers: whether the 10M deposit applies inside the Kiwoom ISA, whether KIS lists the E-nano S&P 500 contract, the KIS commission per contract, and whether KIS pays interest on margin deposits.
honest_ceiling:
No leveraged-index timing method gets to 30-60% a year as a long-run expectation. The realistic expectation is 8-14% net a year (central about 10-11%). A good but plausible outcome is 15-20%. 25% or more needs a repeat of an era like 2010-2021.

Arithmetic. Long-run log growth is approximately: cash rate + k(2 - k) * S^2 / 2 - frictions - tax, where S is the annual Sharpe ratio of the timed exposure and k the fraction of full Kelly leverage.

Sharpe ratios:
- Index buy-and-hold: 0.30-0.45 (S&P 500 1928-2015 measured 0.30 in the Gayed-Bilello study).
- With trend and volatility sizing: about 0.6 in-sample; 0.45-0.55 is a realistic forward figure after shrinkage.

Growth at full Kelly (k = 1):
- S = 0.5 (portfolio volatility 50%): 3% cash + 12.5% - 2.5% (financing spread, fees, trading, idle collateral) - 1.5% (gaps, fat tails, one-day delay) = 11.5% before tax. Tax at 9.9-11% with no loss carry-forward takes 1-2pp. Net about 9.5-10.5% a year.
- S = 0.6: 3 + 18 - 4 = 17% before tax; net about 14.5-15%.
- S = 0.7 (the best in-sample figure): 3 + 24.5 - 4.5 = 23% before tax; net about 19-20%.

What the wish requires:
- 30% net: S of about 0.8-0.9 held at full Kelly (80-90% annual volatility) with the parameters known exactly.
- 60% net: S of about 1.05-1.2.
No long-only index-timing rule has shown that outside a selected window.

Tax is not a flat haircut. With no loss carry-forward, 22% on a 45%-volatility strategy costs about 4pp of log growth a year at 100M KRW and about 2pp at 10M, where the 2.5M exemption covers a quarter of the capital. At 11% on a 30%-volatility strategy it is about 1.5pp. In the ISA it is under 1pp.

Where the 30-60% figures come from: 3x Nasdaq-100 returned roughly 50% a year in 2010-2021, with near-zero rates and the best run of the best major index. The same product over 2000-2002 would have lost about 99%, and any 3x Japanese index after 1989 was wiped out. Those windows are one draw from a distribution whose centre is near 10%.

My probabilities for the best design here over 20 years: at least 30% net a year, under 5%; at least 20%, about 15%; below 5%, about 25%. For scale, 10M KRW at 10% for 20 years becomes about 67M; at 15%, about 164M.
assumptions_challenged:
1. "3x is the growth-maximising multiple." Optimal leverage is expected excess return divided by variance, so it is a moving number. On the S&P 500 it is above 3x in calm uptrends and near 1x when volatility is 25-30%. A fixed 3x with only a trend filter is at 1.5-2 times Kelly in volatile uptrends, and a -20% day costs it 60%.

2. "The trend filter is the timing signal." Most of its historical value comes from volatility being nearly twice as high below the 200-day average (26.5% against 14.7%). Volatility is the more direct state variable; trend adds protection in slow bear markets and costs money in V-shaped recoveries.

3. "Volatility decay is a flaw of leveraged ETFs." It is the variance cost of constant leverage (L^2 * variance / 2) and applies equally to daily-rebalanced futures. The remedy is less leverage when variance is high, not a different product.

4. "The Nasdaq-100 is the index to lever." That is hindsight. On an equal-Sharpe prior the index should be chosen by vehicle cost, tax and liquidity. Test the same rule on Japan, Germany, the UK and Korea to see what it does without US hindsight.

5. "Tax is a fixed percentage." With no loss carry-forward it is convex: the effective rate on a volatile strategy is 1.3-1.5 times the statutory rate. The exemptions are fixed won amounts, so the best vehicle depends on capital. At 10M KRW tax is nearly irrelevant and access rules decide; at 100M tax location is the largest controllable item.

6. "Futures are cheaper than leveraged ETFs." Only if the collateral earns interest. Idle margin at 0% costs about 0.6 times the cash rate, roughly 2% a year, more than the ETF fee it avoids.

7. "Commissions are small." At 0.25% per side, five round trips a year cost 2.5% of capital. Korea-listed ETFs at about 0.015% are more than ten times cheaper and should be considered before any US-listed product.

8. "Backtests on TQQQ since 2010 are evidence." That window had near-zero financing and an exceptional index. At a 5% short rate a 3x fund pays about 11-12% a year in financing and fees. Tests need simulated products back to 1926 and 1985 with actual rates.

9. "Overnight-only exposure is free return." Considered and rejected. The historical close-to-open premium of roughly 5% a year over cash per unit of exposure needs two trades a day. At a Korean retail rate of about USD 5 per Micro round trip on USD 37,750 that is about 1.4 basis points a day, or 3.5% a year, before 11% tax. The margin is too thin, and a US ETF built on this idea closed within about a year.

10. "The rules are stable." In 2026 alone: a 10M KRW deposit for first-time buyers of overseas leveraged ETFs (22 May), a 30M KRW cash deposit for single-stock leveraged products (31 July), and a proposal to cap the ISA at 5 years (3 August, under review).

ideas.name: K-NEGLECT: quiet Korean micro-caps (low turnover, low volatility, no dilution), price data only, gains untaxed
ideas.mechanism: Edge: in Korean small caps the stocks retail traders churn (high turnover, lottery-like jumps, frequent share issuance) are overpriced, and the quiet ones are underpriced. Evidence checked: a KOSPI+KOSDAQ study for 1997-2016 finds high-turnover stocks underperform and that turnover absorbs the idiosyncratic-volatility effect; Nartea, Wu and Liu (2014) find high-MAX stocks lag low-MAX stocks by about 1.9% a month equal-weighted in Korea; net share issuance predicts low returns internationally (McLean, Pontiff and Watanabe 2009, cited from memory). Other side of the trade: retail day-traders who pay up for theme stocks, and the issuers who sell new shares and convertibles to them. Why it should persist: stocks of roughly 25-150bn KRW market cap trading 0.1-1bn KRW a day cannot absorb institutional money, have no analyst coverage, and the overpriced side is impractical to short. A 4M KRW position is about 4% of one day's trading, so a sub-100M KRW account is the size that fits. Structural help: capital gains on listed Korean shares are untaxed for anyone below the large-shareholder line (kept at 5bn KRW per stock in Sept 2025); the only levy is the 0.20% sell tax. Reason for a haircut: a replication of 148 Korean anomalies found only 28-38% significant, with results depending heavily on micro-caps and weighting.
ideas.instruments: KOSPI and KOSDAQ common shares between the 5th and 50th percentile of market cap (about 25-150bn KRW today). Kiwoom ordinary brokerage account, because gains are already untaxed there; keep the ISA for taxable Korea-listed ETFs and use it for this only if there is spare room (it would shelter the roughly 2% dividend yield, worth about 0.3% a year). No leverage: Kiwoom margin loans cost about 9.1% beyond 90 days and many micro-caps are not marginable.
ideas.rule:
All inputs use data up to and including signal day t. r_d = FLUC_RT/100.

ELIGIBLE on day t if all hold: (a) listed on KOSPI or KOSDAQ; (b) common share: short code ends in 0 and does not start with 9 (foreign issuers), base-info SECUGRP_NM = 주권 and KIND_STKCERT_TP_NM = 보통주 where available, name does not contain 스팩, 기업인수목적 or 리츠; (c) KOSDAQ SECT_TP_NM does not contain 관리종목, 투자주의환기, SPAC or 외국기업; (d) at least 250 trading days of history; (e) close >= 1,000 KRW; (f) volume > 0 on each of the last 20 days and on at least 240 of the last 250; (g) median daily traded value over the last 60 days >= 100M KRW; (h) market-cap percentile between 5 and 50 among all stocks passing (a)-(b); (i) ISS <= 0.10.

SIGNALS: TO = mean over 120 days of ACC_TRDVAL / MKTCAP. VOL = standard deviation of r_d over 250 days. ISS (net share issuance) = ln(MKTCAP_t / MKTCAP_t-250) minus the sum over 250 days of ln(1 + r_d). Score = simple average of the three cross-sectional percentile ranks within the eligible set, low is good; ties go to the smaller market cap.

CALENDAR: t = 10th trading day of each month (deliberately off the month-end that retail screeners use). Orders go into the closing auction on t+1.

PORTFOLIO: N = 25 names (20 if equity is under 20M KRW). Monthly: sell any holding whose score rank is worse than 3N, or that fails (b), (c), (e) or (i), or whose market-cap percentile is above 70 or below 3, or whose 60-day median traded value is under 50M KRW. Then buy the best-ranked eligible names not held until N are held, each new position sized at equity / N; skip a name if one share costs more than 1.5 times that amount. Trim any holding above 2.5 x equity / N back to equity / N. Daily: if a holding becomes flagged under (c) or closes below 1,000 KRW, sell in the next closing auction. No stop-loss, no market-timing filter, no leverage; idle cash earns zero in the test.

HALTS AND DELISTINGS: a halted stock is held and marked at its last price. A stock that leaves the data is valued at its last close that had volume > 0; if none of its final 20 rows traded, value it at zero.

TEST COSTS: commission 0.015% a side; sell tax at the historical rate (0.30% to May 2019, 0.25% to 2020, 0.23% in 2021-22, 0.20% in 2023, 0.18% in 2024, 0.15% in 2025, 0.20% in 2026; confirm the dates); slippage 0.5% a side against the t+1 close, with a 1.0% stress run; fill at most 10% of that day's traded value and carry the rest to the next day.

PRE-REGISTRATION: one specification, no parameter search. In-sample Feb 2011-Dec 2014 is a sanity check only (active return over the equal-weight eligible universe must be positive). Holdout Jan 2015 to latest passes if net compound growth is at least the equal-weight eligible universe plus 2% a year and at least a KOSPI 200 total-return ETF. Report as robustness only, never to choose: N = 15 and 40, each signal dropped in turn, liquidity floor 50M and 200M, month-end signal day.
ideas.data:
KRX Open API (openapi.krx.co.kr). Key issued after sign-up and per-service approval; terms are non-commercial use, 10,000 calls a day, yearly renewal. I could not confirm on the terms page that it is free of charge, so check that first. Endpoints /sto/stk_bydd_trd and /sto/ksq_bydd_trd return the whole market for one date (ISU_CD, ISU_NM, SECT_TP_NM, TDD_CLSPRC, FLUC_RT, TDD_OPNPRC, ACC_TRDVOL, ACC_TRDVAL, MKTCAP, LIST_SHRS); /sto/stk_isu_base_info and /sto/ksq_isu_base_info give SECUGRP_NM, KIND_STKCERT_TP_NM and LIST_DD. History starts in 2010; the full pull is about 8,300 calls, one day's quota.

Bias notes: (1) Survivorship is avoided because the universe is built only from rows present on day t in date-keyed snapshots, and delisting losses come from the last traded price or zero. First build step: confirm a stock delisted around 2013-14 appears in earlier snapshots. (2) Check that SECT_TP_NM and base-info are as-of-date values, not today's; if they are today's, using them is look-ahead, so drop those filters in the test. (3) No dividends in the data, so results are understated by roughly 1.5-2% a year. (4) FLUC_RT must be checked around capital reductions, relistings and liquidation trading, since both returns and the ISS signal depend on it.

Sources: https://openapi.krx.co.kr/contents/OPP/INFO/OPPINFO005.jsp ; https://docs.rs/crate/krx-rs/latest/source/src/api/stock.rs ; https://docs.rs/crate/krx-rs/latest/source/src/data/stock.rs ; https://ideas.repec.org/a/eme/ijoemp/ijoem-09-2021-1499.html ; https://ideas.repec.org/a/taf/apfiec/v24y2014i6p425-435.html ; https://repository.hanyang.ac.kr/handle/20.500.11754/167239
ideas.testable_to_2014: Partly. Free survivorship-free Korean data begins 4 Jan 2010, so after the 250-day lookback the in-sample period is only Feb 2011-Dec 2014 (about 4 years) and the holdout is Jan 2015 to now (about 11.8 years). Nothing free and survivorship-free exists before 2010. Statistical power is low: with about 8% tracking error against the universe, a true 4% a year edge gives a t-statistic of only about 1.7 on the holdout, so the test can reject a gross failure but cannot prove the edge.
ideas.expected_net: Arithmetic: cash 2.75% + beta 0.75 x equity premium 4.5% (3.4%) + edge 3-6% (published spreads halved for decay, crowding and micro-cap dependence) = 9-12% gross total return. Less dividend tax 0.3% and trading cost 1.2% (about 100% one-way turnover x 1.23% round trip: 0.20% tax + 0.03% commission + 1.0% slippage) = 7.6-10.6% net arithmetic. Less variance drag 1.6% (18% volatility) = about 6-9% net compound growth, central 8%. If the historical spread held at full strength: 11-13%. Capital gains tax: zero. Sharpe about 0.35-0.55. Expected worst drawdown -45% to -60% in a 2008-type event; Korean small caps fell 35-40% in March 2020.
ideas.capital_fit: 10M KRW: works; 20 names at 0.5M each, and names whose single share costs over 0.75M are skipped. 50M KRW: works; 25 names at 2M each. 100M KRW: works; 4M per name is about 4% of a day's trading at the liquidity floor, so fills take 1-3 closing auctions. Practical ceiling about 0.5-1bn KRW.
ideas.fake_risks: 1. Look-ahead if the administrative-issue flag or base-info is served as today's value rather than the historical one. 2. Wrong handling of FLUC_RT around capital reductions, relistings or liquidation trading creates fake returns and a fake issuance signal. 3. Closing-auction fills in thin names may cost more than 0.5%; the result must survive 1.0%. 4. If the snapshot omits halted stocks, the code could treat a halt as a delisting, or the reverse. 5. Regime luck: quiet small caps did well in 2010-17 and Korean small caps were roughly flat in 2018-24, so the holdout may show little. 6. Crowding from Korean retail screeners running similar small-cap filters. 7. The in-sample period had 15% daily price limits (30% from June 2015), a different microstructure. 8. Four years of in-sample data and one holdout cannot separate a 3% edge from zero.

ideas.name: K-DART: profitable, cheap, improving Korean micro-caps from regulatory filings (data only from 2016)
ideas.mechanism: Edge: among neglected Korean small caps, cheap and profitable companies with rising operating profit are slow to re-rate because nobody covers them and quarterly results arrive only through the statutory filing, not through analyst previews. Other side: retail holders who sell dull stocks to chase themes, and institutions barred by size and liquidity limits. Why it should persist: capacity is a few hundred million KRW per name at most, and filings for these companies are read late. Value and quality are the best-documented Korean small-cap effects in practitioner work, but that evidence comes from paid databases and I did not verify the numbers in this session. Possible tailwind, not an edge: the 2024-26 shareholder-return reforms may re-rate low price-to-book companies once; that would flatter a test without proving anything.
ideas.instruments: Same universe and account as idea 1: KOSPI and KOSDAQ common shares between the 5th and 50th market-cap percentile, Kiwoom ordinary brokerage account, no leverage. Financial companies excluded.
ideas.rule:
UNIVERSE: idea 1 conditions (a) to (i), plus exclude financials (DART induty_code starting 64, 65 or 66) and require a periodic report received no more than 200 days before t.

POINT-IN-TIME RULE: a filing may be used only from the trading day after its receipt date, which is the first 8 digits of rcept_no. Use consolidated statements (CFS) where they exist, otherwise separate (OFS). Prior-period figures are taken from the comparative columns of the same filing, never from a later filing.

INPUTS: B = equity attributable to owners (fallback total equity). A = total assets. L = total liabilities. TTM figures for revenue, gross profit GP, operating income OI and net income attributable to owners NI = latest cumulative year-to-date + last annual figure - prior-year same-period cumulative figure. If gross profit is missing use revenue minus cost of sales, and if that is missing use OI.

HARD FILTERS: OI_ttm > 0, NI_ttm > 0, L / B < 2.0.

SCORES (cross-sectional percentile ranks within the eligible set, high is good): V1 = B / MKTCAP; V2 = NI_ttm / MKTCAP; Q = GP_ttm / A; G = (OI_ttm - OI_ttm one year earlier) / A one year earlier. Composite = equal-weight average of the four ranks.

CALENDAR: four signal days a year, the close of the 3rd trading day after each statutory deadline (31 March, 15 May, 14 August, 14 November). Trade in the next day's closing auction.

PORTFOLIO: N = 25 equal weight (20 if equity is under 20M KRW). Sell when composite rank is worse than 3N or any hard filter or idea 1 exit condition fails; buy the best-ranked names not held up to N; new positions sized at equity / N. Daily event exits, halt and delisting treatment and cost assumptions exactly as idea 1.

PRE-REGISTRATION: the rule is frozen before any data is pulled and run once on April 2016 to latest. Pass if net compound growth is at least the equal-weight eligible universe plus 3% a year and at least idea 1 over the same dates. No parameter may be changed after the run.
ideas.data:
OpenDART API (opendart.fss.or.kr), free key, about 20,000 calls a day, at most 100 companies per multi-company query. Structured financial statements exist only from fiscal year 2015. Endpoint fnlttSinglAcntAll with corp_code, bsns_year, reprt_code (11013 Q1, 11012 half-year, 11014 Q3, 11011 annual) and fs_div. Quarterly and half-year reports are due within 45 days and annual reports within 90 days. A full pull is about 105,000 calls, roughly 6 days. Prices, market cap and shares come from the KRX Open API as in idea 1.

Bias notes: (1) Amended filings: the API can return corrected figures, which is restatement look-ahead; take the original receipt date from list.json and run a sensitivity that drops any company-period with an amendment. (2) Coverage of companies since delisted, and the mapping from old stock codes to corp_code, must be measured; report the share of universe-months with missing statements. Source: https://algolab.co.kr/blog/dart-opendart-financial-statement-api-lag-2026
ideas.testable_to_2014: No. Free structured Korean fundamentals start with fiscal year 2015, so the first signal is April 2016 and nothing can be tested up to 2014. The whole history (about 10.6 years) is therefore a single blind run of a rule fixed in advance from pre-2015 published evidence. Parsing older annual reports from raw DART documents is possible in principle but error-prone and I do not recommend it. Power is low: a 5% a year edge with 9% tracking error gives a t-statistic of about 1.8.
ideas.expected_net: Arithmetic: cash 2.75% + beta 0.85 x 4.5% (3.8%) + edge 5-8% (practitioner backtests of 10-15% a year roughly halved) = 11.5-14.5% gross. Less dividend tax 0.3% and trading cost 1.1% = 10-13% net arithmetic. Less variance drag 2.2% (21% volatility) = about 8-11% net compound growth, central 9.5%. Capital gains tax: zero. Sharpe about 0.35-0.5. Expected worst drawdown -50% to -65%. Correlation with idea 1 is high (about 0.8), so the two are alternatives, not diversifiers.
ideas.capital_fit: 10M KRW: works (20 names). 50M KRW: works. 100M KRW: works, with the same 1-3 day fills as idea 1. Practical ceiling about 0.5-1bn KRW.
ideas.fake_risks: 1. Restated figures served by the API in place of the originally filed ones. 2. Missing statements for failed companies quietly remove the losers from the candidate list. 3. No in-sample period at all: one run, one outcome, and any second run after seeing the first is data mining. 4. The 2024-26 re-rating of low price-to-book stocks may be a one-off that inflates the result. 5. The same screens are popular with Korean retail quant tools, so the effect may already be weaker than in the pre-2017 literature. 6. Micro-cap accounting errors and one-off gains can pollute the net-income rank; the operating-profit filter only partly protects against this.

ideas.name: K-SPAC: Korean blank-cheque shells bought below trust value (cash sleeve, not a growth engine)
ideas.mechanism: Edge: a Korean SPAC places at least 90% (in practice close to 100%) of its IPO money in trust at roughly bank-deposit rates and must return principal plus interest if no merger closes within 3 years. Bought below trust value per share it is a short deposit plus a free option on a merger announcement. Other side: IPO subscribers who sell after listing because nothing happens, and holders who need cash. Why it persists: each shell is about 8-30bn KRW and trades only tens of millions of KRW a day, so it is useless to anyone with real money, and the payoff is too small for retail traders to care. Gains on market sales are untaxed, whereas a deposit pays 15.4% on interest.
ideas.instruments: KOSDAQ-listed SPACs (names containing 스팩; typical IPO price 2,000 KRW, a few at 10,000 KRW). Kiwoom ordinary brokerage account or the ISA. No leverage.
ideas.rule:
UNIVERSE: rows whose ISU_NM contains 스팩 or 기업인수목적 (KOSDAQ SECT_TP_NM contains SPAC), from the listing day.

STATIC TABLE (built once): listing date and IPO price P0 for each SPAC.

FLOOR: F_t = P0 x (1 + 0.8 x average Bank of Korea base rate since listing x years since listing). In live trading replace this with the trust balance per share in the latest DART periodic report, less 0.5%.

ENTRY: if at the close of day t the price is <= 0.99 x F_t, the SPAC has been listed between 20 trading days and 33 months, and it is not halted, place a day limit buy on t+1 at the lower of the day-t close and 0.99 x F_t rounded down to the tick. In the test a fill counts only if the t+1 low is strictly below the limit, and only for up to 10% of that day's volume. Repeat daily while the condition holds, up to 8% of equity per SPAC and 12 positions; unfilled cash stays idle.

EXIT: (1) close >= 1.06 x F_t: sell at the next open (test price: open x 0.995). (2) After a merger-announcement halt (3 or more consecutive zero-volume days) ends: if the resumption close is >= F_t sell at the next open, otherwise keep and apply (1) or (3). If the name ever loses 스팩 (the merged company has replaced it), sell at the next open. (3) From 34 months after listing: sell in the closing auction if close >= 0.997 x F_t; otherwise hold to delisting and book F_t less 15.4% tax on the gain.

COSTS: commission 0.015% a side and 0.20% sell tax.

PRE-REGISTRATION: in-sample 2010-2014, holdout 2015 to latest. Pass if the holdout net return on deployed capital is at least the Bank of Korea base rate plus 1.5% a year with a worst drawdown no deeper than 5%.
ideas.data:
KRX Open API daily snapshots as in idea 1 (SPACs are included from 2010). IPO prices from the exchange's KIND new-listing table or DART issuance reports; I did not confirm that the KIND table downloads without a login, so check that. Base rate from the Bank of Korea ECOS free key or FRED.
